Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
There are (at least) two properties that we could use to define
<TEXTITOPEN_0001>generically finite<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> morphisms. These correspond to whether you
want the property to be local on the source or local on the target:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> (Local on the target; suggested by Ravi Vakil.)
Assume every quasi-compact open of <MATH_0002> has finitely
many irreducible components (for example if <MATH_0003> is locally Noetherian).
The requirement is that the inverse image of each generic point is finite, see
Lemma <REF_0001>.
<STRUCT_0003> (Local on the source.) The requirement is that there exists
a dense open <MATH_0004> such that <MATH_0005> is locally quasi-finite.

In case (1) the requirement can be formulated without the auxiliary

quasi-compact and <MATH_0008> is as in (1) then it does.
